faqs.a: Each card shows the code point (like U+200B) and a description. Zero Width Space is the most invisible. Hangul Filler (U+3164) is the famous one for blank game nicknames. Try pasting each into your target app to see which one it accepts.
faqs.q: Which invisible character should I use?

faqs.a: Some apps strip zero-width characters on purpose to stop abuse. Try the Hangul Filler (U+3164) or Braille Blank (U+2800) instead - they survive in far more apps. The builder lets you test quickly.
faqs.q: The game still says my name is empty. What now?

faqs.a: Technically no - the field contains characters, they are just invisible. Some apps detect and reject them anyway. Use them for fun and formatting, not to bypass rules that matter.
faqs.q: Is using an invisible name cheating?

faqs.a: These are real Unicode characters with real code points. Screen readers may announce some as 'blank' or skip them, which can confuse blind users. Avoid them in public content where accessibility matters.
faqs.q: Do invisible characters cause accessibility problems?

faqs.a: No. Copying from here is the safe way: you get exactly the character shown on the card. Random sites sometimes bundle hidden extra characters or even malicious text.
faqs.q: Can I just copy these from any website?

faqs.a: Yes. Everything runs in your browser. Nothing is uploaded or tracked.

invisible-character.formula:

invisible-character.workedExample:
Making a blank game nickname with Hangul Filler:
1. Find the 'Hangul Filler' card (code point U+3164).
2. In the builder, select Hangul Filler and set Repeat to 3.
3. The bundle is 3 characters long: U+3164 U+3164 U+3164.
4. Click 'Copy bundle' and paste into the game's name field.
5. The name field shows blank, but it contains 3 real characters, so 'empty name' validation passes.

If the game strips it, try the Braille Blank (U+2800) card instead - different apps filter different characters.
